messages:
alex: Quick q — opened a tiny PR that updates the shared JSON schema in `schemas/service-config.yaml`. Not changing runtime behavior, just tightening validation. Who is allowed to approve changes that touch files covered by CODEOWNERS? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/472
meera: +1. If it touches `schemas/shared/**` and service dirs, we usually need owners from both sides. Can you paste the CODEOWNERS snippet you think applies?
alex: sure, looks like this in the repo root:
```
/schemas/shared/** @eng-platform @eng-runtime
/services/model-serving/** @eng-runtime
/docs/** @devex
```
jonathan: For anything that could affect runtime parsing we want an eng-runtime reviewer. For schema semantics, eng-platform should sign off. Practically we want at least one approval from each team listed in the matching CODEOWNERS entry.
lisa: I can review the schema semantics today. @jonathan can you do a quick runtime compatibility pass after I finish? :eyes:
jonathan: Yep — I'll run the local validation tests and smoke the model service. Should be <30m.
sam: Heads-up: if the change is just validation tightening it may block older clients. Add a changelog note and a migration strategy (or a flag) if it's breaking.
alex: good point — I added a test + a short migration note in the PR description. Also explicitly tagged @eng-platform and @eng-runtime in the PR to avoid routing confusion.
merge-bot: Note: repo auto-merge requires 2 approvals or matching CODEOWNERS approval depending on branch protection.
deploy-bot: Reminder: even with approvals, auto-merge is gated on CI passing and a 30m merge window for canary scheduling.
meera: If you want to expedite, mark the review as "priority" in the PR and ping the oncall reviewer, but maintainers still need to approve.
alex: thanks — I'll wait for jonathan + lisa approvals before merging. If anything blocks, I'll open a short rollback plan. thx everyone :pray:
thread_text: (Slack thread about who can approve a schema change; includes CODEOWNERS snippet and PR link)
